heroHeadline: Run the servers you already pay for. See them from the outside and from the box.
heroSub: Sinexis attaches to infrastructure you already run: exposure scan and scheduled checks, one thin agent for on-box inventory and alerts, reachability probes, a public status page, and an AI gateway on the same account. Each service is honest about what it does not do.
honestyBand: Not a pentest. Not a 24/7 SOC. Not a second agent. Not an edge WAF. If a control needs a human or a contract, we say so.
stepConnectDesc: Connect one surface you already run: a host, a domain, a mobile build, or a machine with the agent.
stepWatchDesc: Schedule the scan, attach the agent, or add a probe so the surface stays checked on an interval.
stepProveDesc: Read the diff, the report, or the public status page. Hand the same evidence to a client or an auditor.
faqAuthQ: Do I need written permission to scan?
faqAuthA: Yes. Scan only hosts, domains, and apps you own or are authorized in writing to test. If you run a property or a client rack, get that paper before the first run. Unauthorized scanning is not allowed.
faqPentestQ: Does a human review every finding?
faqPentestA: No. This is automated outside-in scanning on a schedule. It finds exposed services, weak TLS, missing headers, and known CVEs, and it explains what it did not check. It does not walk business logic, chained abuse, or your booking flow. If a contract still needs a manual security audit, keep that engagement and use this between those dates.
faqDataA: Findings and reports stay in your workspace, visible to members you invite. Retention is in the privacy policy. Do not upload credentials or secrets you are not allowed to store off your own systems.
faqGuardQ: How is Guard different from SIEM and Host Protect?
faqGuardA: Guard is the thin agent view: machine inventory plus critical alerts, no log-hunting UI. SIEM is log search plus Cases, which are incident tickets in our Postgres, off by default, not sold live here. Host Protect is a helper on the VM that reads web directories for on-box malware. If the helper is missing or a path is unreachable, we say so and return no hits. We do not invent malware to fill a screen.
faqAgentQ: Two agents on the same VM?
faqAgentA: No. One wazuh-agent per machine, enrolled once to your org. Host Protect is a helper script on that same machine, not a second daemon competing for the box.
faqAiQ: Is AI Gateway a security product?
faqAiA: No. It is a Beta utility on the same account: one wallet and API keys for your team's models. It is not part of the security claim, and it does not make the scan, Guard, or uptime results stronger.
